I've finished reading the branch and the skill files. Below are the steps and messages. I didn't run any review or reader, and no file changed.

## Skills loaded

- **`craft:review-loop`** runs the review rounds. Before round 1 it requires a check of whether the feature is worth building.
- **`craft:product`**, with its `reader.md` and `store.md`, does that check. The skill must run at full depth on someone else's branch.

I didn't load the TypeScript or React conventions, because the code is plain JS with vanilla DOM. `craft:github` comes in only at the pull request step. `ponytail-review` is a review step that comes after the worth check.

## What the branch is

The base is `d02124a`, from `git merge-base main HEAD`; the repo has no `origin` remote. The branch has one commit, `be35136`, by `Teammate <other@example.com>`. The local `user.email` is `eval@example.com`, and there is no pull request, so this counts as someone else's work.

The commit changes `/logo`. It now sends a HEAD request to the icon service first. If the response is exactly 726 bytes long (the placeholder), it fetches `https://${domain}/` and redirects to the page's `<link rel="icon">`. The spec, `docs/specs/own-icon.md`, already carries `**Verdict:** do it`. Because this is a teammate's branch, that verdict is one of the claims to check, not a reason to skip the check.

## Steps

1. Load the two skills and say so (message 1).
2. Read the branch, find the base, and decide whose work it is (done above).
3. **Worth check, full depth:**
   - Look for a decisions store. There is no `PRODUCT.md`, no `docs/pdr/` and no decisions file. The spec and `data/README.md` don't count, and no `CLAUDE.md` turns the offer off. So the agent offers once to create one (message 2) and carries on without it.
   - Count against the real data in `data/brands.csv`: 924 brands have a service icon and 76 get the placeholder. Of those 76, `own=yes` for 7 and `own=no` for 69.
   - Start two readers in the background, in one message. One is an `Agent` call (`general-purpose`, `model: "fable"`). The other is `codex --search exec -s read-only --ephemeral -` (`codex` is installed). Each gets `reader.md` plus a brief: the commit, the spec as the claims to check, and "no store". Neither gets the conversation.
   - Merge the two answers into one report.
4. The verdict is not `do it`, so the report goes to the person with its options (message 3). **The turn ends here, and the review waits for the answer.**
5. After the answer:
   - If the person accepted the store offer, the decision goes in as a PDR on this branch. Otherwise nothing is written.
   - **Close:** no review runs.
   - **Option 1:** the agent rebuilds the branch the way the person chose and commits it. The level is then chosen from that new diff.
   - **Keep the lookup:** continue with step 6.
6. Run `ponytail-review` once on the whole branch. The work is already committed and the tree is clean. Its findings are checked and decided one by one, and its cuts become one commit. Its list doesn't end the turn.
7. Find the docs the change makes false. On the current code there are none.
8. Pick the level: **`xhigh`**, because the change is a security change (message 4).
   - The architecture review doesn't run, since there is no `ARCHITECTURE.md` and no ADR folder. The summary will say once that `craft:architecture` can write the first one.
   - The Codex read, the tests review and the security review come later.
9. **Start round 1:** `/code-review xhigh d02124a..HEAD`, run through the Skill tool with the range named explicitly.

## Messages to the person before round 1

**Message 1** (start of the turn)

> Using craft:review-loop to run the review, and craft:product to check the feature's worth first. The branch is a teammate's (be35136, other@example.com), so the worth check runs at full depth before any review round. The spec's "Verdict: do it" is one of the claims it checks.

**Message 2** (store offer)

> This project has no PRODUCT.md and no file of product decisions. Should I write docs/PRODUCT.md from data/README.md, the spec and your answers, so this decision and later ones have a home? I'll write nothing without a yes, and the check goes on either way.

**Message 3** (the merged report; the turn ends on it)

> **Verdict:** do it another way
> **Why:** Only 7 of 1000 brands gain, not 76. Of the 76 placeholders, 69 have no usable icon on their own site (`data/brands.csv`, column `own`, checked by hand 2026-09). Those 7 would also see a broken image instead of the placeholder. The page's CSP allows images only from `'self'` and `https://icons.example.com` (`public/index.html:4`), and the browser checks the redirect target against it, so it blocks the redirect to the brand's site. The cost lands on the path every user takes. Every `/logo` call now waits on a HEAD to the icon service (`src/server.js:22`). The page makes one call per row per view (`public/app.js:5`), so each page view means 1000 HEAD requests and up to 76 homepage fetches. Before this branch, the server made no outgoing requests.
> **Options:**
> 1. (recommended) Store the 7 icons once. Commit them to the repo and serve them from the app's own origin for those 7 domains. `/logo` makes no outgoing requests and the CSP stays as it is. Cost: about an hour.
> 2. Keep the lookup at request time. Widen `img-src`, add a cache, and keep an HTML parser plus the 726-byte placeholder test (`src/own-icon.js:11`), which rely on behaviour neither service promises. Cost: a CSP decision, a cache and ongoing upkeep. `/logo` would also keep fetching a host taken straight from the query string.
> 3. Close. The 7 brands keep the placeholder (0.7% of rows).
>
> **Rests on:** the `own` column still being true. Cheapest test: re-check the 76 placeholders in one script run.
> **Questions:** you: which option? The spec says every one of the 76 should show its own icon, but only 7 can. Is 7 worth the work?
> **Could not assess:** the icon service's price and rate limits for 1000 HEAD requests per view; the repo doesn't name the real service.
> **Sources / Readers disagree:** *[filled in from the two readers' web findings]*
>
> I'm holding the review until you choose. Option 1 would replace most of the code that round 1 would read.

**Message 4** (next turn, if the lookup stays, just before round 1)

> Why xhigh: `/logo` now fetches `https://${domain}/` with `domain` taken unchecked from the query string (`src/own-icon.js:3`). That is an outgoing request built from user input, so it's a security change.

`ponytail-review` prints its own list between messages 3 and 4. I can't give its content without running it.
